metadata.title: My Paper Had Fake Citations
metadata.audience: Students and practitioners learning to use and report on AI systems
metadata.fellow: Janvi Chitroda, AI Data Engineer volunteer, Medhavy project, Humanitarians AI
metadata.source: inbox/term2-week09/term2-week9-video-content.md (Week 9); narration supplied verbatim and pre-approved by Janvi (2026-10-27)
metadata.note: Project update. Thesis: the reference audit is finished — across 24 references, 2 fabricated and 7 with incorrect details (37.5%); both fabricated ones replaced with real papers, every reference given a DOI, a full consistency pass, and a summary of every change sent to all three professors. Irony: a pipeline to check AI-generated definitions, a paper with AI-fabricated citations. The audit and fixes are Janvi's. Only Professor Brown may be named; the professors are not named. Every on-screen number appears in the Week 9 source as written.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer, ask lands answered. Required intro line + AI-narration disclosure.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Janvi and this video is about finishing an audit of our paper's 24 references, and what I found. This narration is an AI-generated voice; the work is mine.

props.command: I need to finish checking the 24 references in my paper. How do I confirm each one is real?
output: Search each exact title in Scholar, Crossref, arXiv
Search a named venue's own proceedings
Add a DOI to every reference

beats.role_note: Reference list [1]–[12] already checked ([6] fabricated); [13]–[24] now highlighted; chips Google Scholar · Crossref · arXiv · proceedings.
beats.narration_text: Last week, the first 12 references turned up one fabricated paper. This week I checked the remaining 12, against Google Scholar, Crossref and arXiv, and the conference proceedings themselves.
beats.visual_intent: Reference list [1]–[12] already checked ([6] fabricated); [13]–[24] now highlighted; chips Google Scholar · Crossref · arXiv · proceedings.

beats.role_note: [14] FABRICATED · 0 matches in BEA 2023 proceedings; [13] wrong initial + title · [15] wrong third author · [19] wrong pages D1009-D1014 → D940-D946.
beats.narration_text: Reference 14 didn't exist either. I searched the full BEA 2023 proceedings on the ACL Anthology and found zero matches. Others had a wrong author initial and title, a wrong third author, and wrong page numbers.
beats.visual_intent: [14] FABRICATED · 0 matches in BEA 2023 proceedings; [13] wrong initial + title · [15] wrong third author · [19] wrong pages D1009-D1014 → D940-D946.

beats.role_note: Total card: 24 references · 2 fabricated · 7 incorrect details · 37.5%.
beats.narration_text: Across all 24, two references were fabricated and seven had incorrect details. That's 37.5 percent.
beats.visual_intent: Total card: 24 references · 2 fabricated · 7 incorrect details · 37.5%.

beats.role_note: Replacement cards: [6] → Mendes et al., 'DBpedia Spotlight', I-Semantics 2011 · [14] → Sarsa et al., 'Automatic generation of programming exercises', ICER 2022; chip 'several searches'.
beats.narration_text: I replaced both fabricated ones with real papers that make the same point: DBpedia Spotlight from 2011, and a 2022 study on automatically generating programming exercises. Both took several searches to find.
beats.visual_intent: Replacement cards: [6] → Mendes et al., 'DBpedia Spotlight', I-Semantics 2011 · [14] → Sarsa et al., 'Automatic generation of programming exercises', ICER 2022; chip 'several searches'.

beats.role_note: Checklist: 7 corrected · DOI on all 24 · in-text citations re-read.
beats.narration_text: Then I corrected the seven, added a DOI to every reference, and checked that each in-text citation still made sense.
beats.visual_intent: Checklist: 7 corrected · DOI on all 24 · in-text citations re-read.

beats.role_note: Consistency checklist ticking: sensitivity 74.0% · 20.7% · 79.3% · ablation 2,046 · 1,799 · 4.5-fold · kappa 0.4884 · 0.3847 · funnel 10,049 → 8,161 → 8,053 · 'curated' throughout · abstract under 300 words; envelope 'all three professors'.
beats.narration_text: Finally, a full consistency pass: every sensitivity, ablation and kappa number, the pipeline funnel, curated instead of verified throughout, and the abstract under 300 words. Then I sent all three professors a summary of every change.
